text:
Priya Shah: RFC follow-up — proposal for a lightweight panel query facade to handle auth, routing and load-shedding for console dashboards. link: https://r.rw/console-query-facade

Priya Shah: TL;DR: thin facade service sits in front of existing query workers. responsibilities: RBAC check, tenant routing, request shaping (max tokens/rows), early load-shed, and short-lived prefix cache. Pros: centralize auth logic, easier rollout of new routing, unified telemetry. Cons: extra network hop, added single-service SLO, more code to maintain.

Mateo Rivera: +1 on centralizing auth. question: where do we do the heavy permission checks (role graph expansions)? facade or downstream? doing it in facade avoids duplicated work but is expensive per request.

Lin Zhao: can we short-circuit expensive expansions with a cached decision keyed by (tenant, route, action)? 1s TTL should cover most interactive dashboard hits. we already have a permission cache in auth-service, can reuse.

Samir Patel: perf numbers I ran: direct fetch -> median 45ms; adding a ~10ms hop (lightweight facade) keeps median < 60ms. but p95 jumps if facade does DB-backed role expansion. need to ensure facade uses cached view or async expansion.

Ravi Krishnan: idea: facade verifies a token (fast), checks a local LRU of permission decisions, if miss -> fetch from auth-service async + return conservative deny or fallback to downstream auth? Not great for UX if denies. alternative: facade returns a 202 and triggers downstream warm path?

Priya Shah: tradeoffs: UX vs safety. we should avoid returning 202 for dashboards. proposal: facade does fast cached checks; on cache-miss it proxies the request to downstream worker which does authoritative check and increments a "cache-warm" metric so we can observe misses. that keeps correctness while limiting expansion work in facade.

Mateo Rivera: sounds reasonable. need explicit metrics: auth_cache_hit, auth_cache_miss_proxy, auth_expansion_latency, facade_p95_latency. Also histogram of payload sizes so we can tune max_rows.

Lin Zhao: load-shedding policy proposal: when backend queueing exceeds X ms or CPU > 80% for 30s, facade should apply graceful degradation rules in order: 1) reduce max_rows 2) force lower-fidelity projection (pre-aggregated) 3) reject with 503 + Retry-After. we already have a circuit-breaker lib; can plug that in.

Samir Patel: +1. need to version degradation rules by tenant tier. enterprise tenants get fewer degradations. config example: 
```json
{
  "tiers": {
    "enterprise": {"max_rows": 2000, "degrade_order": ["projection","rows"]},
    "standard": {"max_rows": 200, "degrade_order": ["rows","reject"]}
  }
}
```

Ravi Krishnan: rollout plan: feature-flag facade per cluster. Start with pass-through mode where facade only logs decisions and metrics, then canary where it enforces only on non-prod namespaces, then staged for low-traffic prod tenants. need runbook for facade OOM/latency.

Priya Shah: agree. operational checklist draft:
- add facade metrics to console dashboards
- add synthetic checks (small panel queries) to SLO monitoring
- add a canary namespace + feature flag gate
- prepare fallback route in service mesh to bypass facade if it becomes unhealthy

Samir Patel: sample curl to test auth cache miss scenario: 
```
curl -v -X POST https://console-proxy.test/query -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"panel_id":123, "rows":500}'
```
check header `x-auth-decision: cached|proxy`.

Lin Zhao: tests: unit for cache TTL logic, integration test with auth-service stub that returns both allow/deny, load test at 10k rps synthetic to validate p95 under degradation policy.

Mateo Rivera: one more: telemetry must include trace id propagation so we can trace extra hop. add `x-trace-id` and hook into our distributed tracing.

Priya Shah: action items:
- Lin: prototype LRU permission cache + metrics (ETA 1w)
- Samir: perf baseline + synthetic load harness for facade (ETA 2w)
- Mateo: add facade metrics to dashboards + tracing (ETA 1w)
- Ravi: write rollout + fallback runbook (ETA 3d)

Ravi Krishnan: noted. I'll create the feature-flag ticket and the initial runbook.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued for cluster: canary-console. started rollout to canary1 at 4278912400. status: success on 1/1 nodes.

Priya Shah: thanks all — will sync Thurs 10am to check progress. :thumbsup:
